V114 versus Prevnar 13: the four solicited injection-site symptoms

In participants randomised to the 15-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine V114 or to the 13-valent comparator Prevnar 13, how does the risk of each solicited injection-site symptom compare?

In this section: Registration and administrative information (PROSPERO field set) · What this object claims to contain

What this object claims to contain

This reports every solicited injection-site symptom these trials post. Not every trial posts every symptom, and each outcome names the trials that contribute to it. It is a local tolerability review and covers neither immunogenicity nor protection against pneumococcal disease.

Not held in this object. No search record is held in this object. The included set was reconciled against published syntheses rather than produced by a database search, so no query, date or yield can be shown. Treat the included set as a convenience sample, not a systematic one.
Not held in this object. No screening log is recorded for this review. The included set was reconciled against published syntheses rather than screened from a search, so no records-identified, excluded-with-reason or dual-screening counts exist.

TSA boundaries depend entirely on a target information size that must be pre-specified. This review's protocol registers none, so any boundary drawn here would be a parameter chosen after seeing the data -- which is the practice TSA exists to protect against.

  1. No GRADE assessment or reconciliation record is held in this object, so the certainty of this evidence has not been rated. This is recorded as a declared departure under Cochrane Handbook §III.3.4.1: the review reports a pooled estimate for which no certainty assessment was made. Rating it here would require two assessors and an adjudicator, and a rating produced by neither is not a GRADE assessment whatever letter it carries.
  2. Read this beside `estimand_established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the same quantity. It records nothing about what that quantity was measured against -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.

Other recorded qualifications

Statements this review records about the limits of what it establishes, which are not shown elsewhere on this page. They are reproduced from the object verbatim and are not summarised.

Table 18. Other recorded qualifications
This object records whether the symptom was registered as present, and nothing about how severe or how long-lasting it was. It says nothing about protection against disease.
Rob2 domain 5 bias in selection of the reported resultHIGH risk for every contributing trial on every one of the four outcomes
Covers bias arising when 'the reported result is selected (based on its direction, magnitude or statistical significance) from among multiple intervention effect estimates that were calculated by the trial authors'.
Relationship to the other defect on this pageThis page carries two independent defects found by different screens on different days. The first: its four injection-site outcomes are classes inside one registered composite, never separate endpoints -- recorded in results.by_outcome[*].poolable_reason and in the 25 endpoint-definition rows on inputs.trials[]. The second, here: None of the eight registrations declares a clinical endpoint at any rank. Neither supersedes the other and both are kept.

In this section: Summary

Summary

Question. In participants randomised to the 15-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine V114 or to the 13-valent comparator Prevnar 13, how does the risk of each solicited injection-site symptom compare?

What was found. 7 registered trials:

Table 19. Summary
RegistrationTrial
NCT02547649Safety, Tolerability, and Immunogenicity of Two Formulations of V114 in Healthy Adults 50 Years of Age or Older (V114-006)
NCT03547167A Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, and Immunogenicity of V114 Followed by PNEUMOVAX™23 in Adults at Increased Risk for Pneumococcal Disease
NCT03950622Safety and Immunogenicity of V114 in Healthy Adults (V114-019/PNEU-AGE)
NCT03620162A Study to Evaluate the Interchangeability of V114 and Prevnar 13™ in Healthy Infants (V114-027/PNEU-DIRECTION)
NCT03692871A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Tolerability of V114 and Prevnar 13™ in Healthy Infants (V114-031/PNEU-LINK)
NCT03848065Safety, Tolerability, and Immunogenicity of V114 in Healthy Japanese Infants (V114-028)
NCT03921424Safety and Immunogenicity of V114 in Children Infected With Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) (V114-030/PNEU-WAY PED)

Why no result is pooled. Not one of the seven trials registers this symptom as an outcome measure. Each registers a single solicited injection-site endpoint -- 'Percentage of Participants With a Solicited Injection-site Adverse Event' or its close variant -- and the individual symptoms appear only as classes inside that measure's posted results.

What would change this. A pooled result becomes possible when trials reporting a shared, comparably measured outcome are available.

No pooled estimate, risk-of-bias assessment or certainty rating is published for this question, because there is no combined result for them to describe.

Not held in this object. No statistical panel set is held in this object.
